Hi June. 15 is not prime. 3 × 5 = 15.
merge_intervals([[8, 10], [1, 3], [2, 6]]). Touching counts. I want the result and the reason the sort matters.

<think>
[frame: pathway=s2|mode=plan|construct=deeptree|persona=neutral|identity=none|theme=none|channel=reasoning]
Unsorted, a left-to-right merge would see [8, 10] first and then fail to absorb [1, 3]. Sort to [[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10]]. 2 <= 3, extend to [1, 6]. 8 > 6, so [8, 10] stays. Result [[1, 6], [8, 10]]. The sort is the whole correctness argument. Without it the algorithm is wrong, not just slow.
</think>

[[1, 6], [8, 10]]. Without the sort, [8, 10] would open first and [1, 3] would look like a separate span.
The library drills don't come back. What's the fix you'd actually try, in a sentence?

Take a deposit, returned with the drill. A reminder doesn't change the cost of keeping it.
